chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Isحاق ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a slave boy of mine who jumped upon a slave girl of mine and impregnated her, so she gave birth, and we needed her milk; for I had permitted them what they did. Is the milk good? He said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Is the milk of a slave girl who bears a child by her master's slave boy considered pure in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the purity of milk from a slave girl who bore her master's slave boy, ruling it permissible for consumption despite the master's prior permission of their union. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the legal status of the parents' relationship and the inherent purity (taharah) of the resulting milk, affirming its suitability for nourishment without requiring further purification.
